messages:
alex: Heads-up — getting a P99 regression from a customer after last night's batcher tweak. p99 went 180ms -> ~1.8s around 03:10 UTC. Looks correlated with continuous-batcher change grace_window=10ms (was 2ms).

maria_support: Which tenant / ticket? I got a P1 from Acme in #support (TKT-8921). They pasted a couple of slow traces.

alex: Tenant acme-co, ticket TKT-8921. metric-bot alerted: 'alert: inference_p99_by_tenant{tenant="acme-co"}=1.85s @ 2026-03-16T03:12Z'

metric-bot: "CPU usage OK. GPU queued: +12% over baseline. batcher_hold_count spike +420 in last 5m."

elias_oncall: @jamie @sarah oncall — can you grab a quick look? I'm patching a canary rollback if easy. :eyes:

jamie: I can reproduce locally with load generator hitting many small prompts (avg token len 6). If grace_window is 10ms we tend to wait and coalesce tiny requests which increases tail for single-token quick calls — head-of-line effect. Repro steps:
```bash
# run 200 qps of tiny prompts
wrk -t4 -c100 -d60s --latency "http://localhost:8080/generate" -s ./scripts/tiny_req.lua
```
Response latency: many requests ~200-400ms extra waiting.

sarah: Found the config diff in git:
```diff
-continuous_batcher:
-  grace_window_ms: 2
+continuous_batcher:
+  grace_window_ms: 10
+  small_request_threshold: 16
```
The small_request_threshold was also set which interacts badly with our small-prompt path.

jamie: Key problem is small_request_threshold made the batcher treat dozens of tiny requests as eligible for batching even if their estimated execution time was tiny too. They sit at head of queue until a larger request arrives to fill batch. Leads to ~10-20x p99 multiplier on those tenants with bursty tiny prompts.

elias_oncall: Plan A: quick rollback the grace_window to 2ms on canary and enable immediate-forward for requests below 32 tokens. Plan B: revert full deploy if canary shows improvement.

deploy-bot: triggered rollout: redeploy inference-service acme-canary -> set env CONT_BATCHER_GRACE_MS=2 CONT_BATCHER_IMMEDIATE_FORWARD_TOKEN_THRESHOLD=32

metric-bot: will monitor. PromQL: sum by(tenant)(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[2m])) by (le, tenant)))

alex: Repro proof: after canary patch I ran the same wrk load — p99 back to ~220ms (from 1.8s). Good sign.

maria_support: I told Acme we're rolling a canary rollback, asked for patience. They appreciate the quick updates. :thumbsup:

jamie: Short-term mitigation notes for postmortem:
- keep grace_window <=3ms for continuous-batcher by default
- add special-case immediate-forward for token_count < 32
- add telemetry for small_batch_hold_time per-tenant
- add unit test that simulates many tiny prompts to ensure no HOL blocking

sarah: Added a draft PR with default tweak + additional metrics: https://git.redwood/inference/PR-5423 — contains tests and dashboards.

elias_oncall: Rolling the change to 100% after 12m canary looks stable. p99 for acme-co at 03:28 UTC: 210ms. Rolling notes: reverted grace_window and enabled immediate-forward for small requests.

deploy-bot: rollout complete: inference-service v1.12.9 -> v1.12.9-hotfix-ctch  (canary -> prod)

maria_support: Sent final update to customer, closed TKT-8921 as 'mitigated, follow-up config change in progress'.

alex: Filing follow-up postmortem + config safe-guards. Thanks @elias_oncall @jamie @sarah for the fast triage.

elias_oncall: I'll own the postmortem draft. Will include root cause (aggressive grace_window + small_request_threshold), mitigations, and next steps. :white_check_mark:

maria_support: marking as resolved in #support and tagging for postmortem review.

jamie: TL;DR — continuous-batcher change increased wait for tiny prompts, caused HOL blocking, reverted and added immediate-forward for tiny tokens.

sarah: Will follow up tomorrow with dashboard links and the PR number in the postmortem.

metric-bot: summary: p99 (acme-co) before: ~180ms, spike: ~1.8s @03:12, after rollback: ~210ms @03:28.
